summary: Before the morning korban could be shechted, a Kohen went to look if it was already day. He called out "Barkai!" which means the sky is bright.

chunks.en: The one in charge said to them,
chunks.st: The appointed priest said to the other priests:

chunks.he: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ אִם הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַשְּׁחִיטָה.
chunks.en: "Go out and see if the time for shechitah has come."
chunks.st: Go out and observe if it is day and the time for slaughter has arrived.

chunks.en: If it had come,
chunks.st: If the time has arrived,

chunks.en: the one who saw it says, "Barkai!"
chunks.st: the observer says: There is light [barkai].

chunks.en: Masisya ben Shmuel says,
chunks.st: Matya ben Shmuel says that the appointed priest phrased his question differently:

chunks.he: הֵאִיר פְּנֵי כָל הַמִּזְרָח עַד שֶׁבְּחֶבְרוֹן.
chunks.en: "Is the whole eastern sky lit up, all the way to Chevron?"
chunks.st: Is the entire eastern sky illuminated even to Hebron?

chunks.en: And he says, "Yes."
chunks.st: And the observer says: Yes.

summary: They checked so carefully because once the moonlight fooled them and they shechted the tamid too early. Then the Kohen Gadol was brought to toivel, because anyone who goes into the azarah to serve must toivel.

chunks.en: And why did they need this?
chunks.st: And why did they need to ascertain whether or not it is day, which is typically evident to all? It was necessary,

chunks.en: Because once the moonlight came up,
chunks.st: as once, the light of the moon rose,

chunks.en: and they thought the east was lit up,
chunks.st: and they imagined that the eastern sky was illuminated with sunlight,

chunks.en: and they shechted the tamid,
chunks.st: and they slaughtered the daily offering before its appropriate time.

chunks.en: and they had to take it out to be burned.
chunks.explain: A korban shechted before daytime is not kosher.
chunks.st: The animal was later taken out to the place designated for burning and burned because it was slaughtered too early.
chunks.stMore: In order to prevent similar errors in the future, the Sages instituted that they would carefully assess the situation until they were certain that it was day.

chunks.en: They brought the Kohen Gadol down to the place for toiveling.
chunks.st: After the priests announced the start of the day, they led the High Priest down to the Hall of Immersion.

chunks.en: This was the rule in the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: The Gemara comments: This was the principle in the Temple:

chunks.he: כָּל הַמֵּסֵךְ אֶת רַגְלָיו טָעוּן טְבִילָה,
chunks.en: Anyone who "covers his feet" must toivel,
chunks.explain: "Covers his feet" is a polite way to say he went to the bathroom.
chunks.st: Anyone who covers his legs, a euphemism for defecating, requires immersion afterward;

chunks.he: וְכָל הַמַּטִּיל מַיִם טָעוּן קִדּוּשׁ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלָיִם:
chunks.en: and anyone who passes water must wash his hands and feet.
chunks.st: and anyone who urinates requires sanctification of the hands and feet with water from the basin afterward.

summary: Nobody may go into the azarah to serve until he toivels. On Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol toivels five times and washes his hands and feet ten times.

chunks.en: No one goes into the azarah for the service,
chunks.st: A person does not enter the Temple courtyard for the Temple service,

words.note: The big courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: even if he is tahor,
chunks.st: even if he is pure,

chunks.en: until he toivels.
chunks.st: until he immerses.

chunks.en: Five tevilos and ten washings
chunks.st: Five immersions and ten sanctifications

words.note: A tevilah is dipping the whole body in a mikveh.
Washing the hands and feet from the kiyor.

chunks.he: טוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: the Kohen Gadol toivels and washes on that day,
chunks.st: the High Priest immerses and sanctifies his hands and feet, respectively, on the day of Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: and all of them are in the holy area, on top of the Parvah room,
chunks.st: And all of these immersions and sanctifications take place in the sacred area, the Temple courtyard, on the roof of the Hall of Parva,

words.note: A room in the Beis HaMikdash with a mikveh on its roof.

chunks.en: except for this one only.
chunks.explain: The first tevilah may be done outside the azarah.
chunks.st: except for this first immersion alone.
chunks.stMore: As that immersion is not unique to Yom Kippur, it may be performed outside the courtyard.

summary: The Kohen Gadol toivels behind a linen sheet, puts on his golden clothes, and does the regular morning service of the korban tamid.

chunks.en: They spread out a sheet of linen
chunks.st: They spread a sheet of fine linen

chunks.en: between him and the people.
chunks.st: between him and the people in the interest of modesty,
chunks.stMore: and then the High Priest immersed and sanctified his hands and feet.

chunks.en: He took off his clothes, went down and toiveled,
chunks.st: The High Priest removed the white garments that he was wearing, descended to the ritual bath, and immersed.

chunks.en: came up and dried himself.
chunks.st: He ascended and dried himself with a towel.

chunks.en: They brought him the golden clothes,
chunks.st: Then they brought him the golden garments of the High Priest,

words.note: The Kohen Gadol's special eight garments, with gold in them.

chunks.en: and he put them on, and washed his hands and his feet.
chunks.st: and he dressed in the garments, and he sanctified his hands and his feet.

chunks.en: They brought him the tamid.
chunks.st: They brought him the sheep for the daily morning offering,

chunks.he: קְרָצוֹ, וּמֵרַק אַחֵר שְׁחִיטָה עַל יָדוֹ.
chunks.en: He cut it, and another Kohen finished the shechitah for him.
chunks.st: which he slaughtered by cutting most of the way through the gullet and the windpipe. And a different priest completed the slaughter on his behalf
chunks.stMore: so that the High Priest could receive the blood in a vessel and proceed with the order of the Yom Kippur service.

chunks.en: He caught the blood and sprinkled it.
chunks.st: As soon as the slaughter was completed, the High Priest received the blood in a vessel and sprinkled it on the altar.

chunks.en: He went in to burn the morning ketores,
chunks.st: He entered the Sanctuary to burn the morning incense

chunks.en: and to clean the lamps,
chunks.st: and to remove the ashes from the lamps of the candelabrum;

chunks.en: and to bring the head and the parts,
chunks.st: and he left the Sanctuary and returned to the courtyard to sacrifice the head and the limbs of the sheep sacrificed for the daily offering

chunks.en: and the griddle-cakes and the wine.
chunks.st: and the High Priest’s daily griddle-cake offering, and the wine libation of the daily offering.

summary: This mishnah tells when the ketores is burned in the morning and in the afternoon. If the Kohen Gadol is old or delicate, they warm the mikveh water for him.

chunks.en: The morning ketores was
chunks.st: The Mishna comments: The morning incense

chunks.en: brought between the blood and the parts.
chunks.st: was burned between the receiving and sprinkling of the blood and the burning of the limbs;

chunks.en: And the afternoon ketores,
chunks.st: and the afternoon incense was burned

chunks.en: between the parts and the nesachim.
chunks.st: between the taking of the limbs up to the altar and the pouring of the libations that accompanied the offering.

words.note: The wine poured on the mizbeach with a korban.

chunks.en: If the Kohen Gadol was
chunks.st: With regard to the immersion, if the High Priest was old and found it difficult to immerse in cold water,

chunks.en: old or delicate,
chunks.st: or if he was delicate [istenis],

chunks.he: מְחַמִּין לוֹ חַמִּין וּמְטִילִין לְתוֹךְ הַצּוֹנֵן,
chunks.en: they heat hot water for him and pour it into the cold mikveh,
chunks.st: they would heat hot water for him on Yom Kippur eve and place it into the cold water of the ritual bath

chunks.en: so that its coldness will go away.
chunks.st: in order to temper its chill so the High Priest could immerse without discomfort.

summary: For the second tevilah, they bring the Kohen Gadol to the Parvah room. He toivels, puts on the white clothes, and washes his hands and feet.

chunks.en: They brought him to the Parvah room,
chunks.st: They brought the High Priest to immerse a second time in the Hall of Parva,

chunks.en: and it was in the holy area.
chunks.st: which was in the sacred area, the Temple courtyard.

chunks.en: They spread out a sheet of linen
chunks.st: They spread a sheet of fine linen

chunks.en: between him and the people.
chunks.st: between him and the people in the interest of modesty.

chunks.en: He washed his hands and his feet, and took off his clothes.
chunks.st: And he sanctified his hands and his feet and removed his garments.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says that this was the sequence:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he took off his clothes, then washed his hands and his feet.
chunks.st: He first removed his garments and then he sanctified his hands and his feet.

chunks.en: He went down and toiveled,
chunks.st: He descended and immersed a second time.

chunks.en: came up and dried himself.
chunks.st: He ascended and dried himself.

chunks.en: They brought him the white clothes,
chunks.explain: On Yom Kippur the special service is done in plain white linen.
chunks.st: And they immediately brought him the white garments,

chunks.en: he put them on and washed his hands and his feet.
chunks.st: in which he dressed, and he sanctified his hands and his feet.

summary: The Kohen Gadol's white linen clothes for Yom Kippur were very expensive. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue how much they cost.

chunks.en: In the morning he would wear Pelusium linen
chunks.st: In the morning he would wear linen garments from the Egyptian city of Pelusium

words.note: Fine linen from the city of Pelusium in Mitzrayim.

chunks.en: worth twelve maneh.
chunks.st: worth twelve maneh, 1,200 dinars or zuz.
chunks.stMore: These garments were very expensive due to their high quality.

words.note: A maneh is one hundred zuz, a lot of money.

chunks.en: And in the afternoon, Indian linen
chunks.st: And in the afternoon he wore linen garments from India, which were slightly less expensive,

chunks.en: worth eight hundred zuz.
chunks.st: worth eight hundred zuz.

words.note: A zuz is a silver coin.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: In the morning he would wear
chunks.st: In the morning he would wear garments

chunks.en: clothes worth eighteen maneh,
chunks.st: worth eighteen maneh,

chunks.he: וּבֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם שֶׁל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה,
chunks.en: and in the afternoon, clothes worth twelve maneh.
chunks.st: and in the afternoon he would wear garments worth twelve maneh.

chunks.en: Altogether, thirty maneh.
chunks.st: In total, the clothes were worth thirty maneh.

chunks.en: These were paid for by the community.
chunks.st: These sums for the garments came from the community,

chunks.en: And if he wanted to add,
chunks.st: and if the High Priest wished to add money to purchase even finer garments,

chunks.en: he adds from his own money.
chunks.st: he would add funding of his own.

summary: The Kohen Gadol leans his hands on his bull and does viduy for himself and his family, asking Hashem to forgive them. Everyone answers "Baruch shem kevod malchuso le'olam va'ed."

chunks.en: He comes to his bull,
chunks.st: The High Priest comes and stands next to his bull,

chunks.he: וּפָרוֹ הָיָה עוֹמֵד בֵּין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
chunks.en: and his bull was standing between the Ulam and the mizbeach,
chunks.st: and his bull was standing between the Entrance Hall and the altar

words.note: The big entrance hall in front of the Heichal.

chunks.en: its head to the south and its face to the west.
chunks.st: with its head facing to the south and its face to the west.

chunks.en: And the Kohen stands on the east, facing west,
chunks.st: And the priest stands to the east of the bull, and his face points to the west.

chunks.en: and leans his two hands on it and says viduy.
chunks.explain: Viduy means saying out loud the sins and being sorry for them.
chunks.st: And the priest places his two hands on the bull and confesses.

chunks.en: And this is what he would say:
chunks.st: And this is what he would say in his confession:

chunks.en: "Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please, God,

chunks.he: עָוִיתִי פָּשַׁעְתִּי חָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי.
chunks.en: I have done wrong, I have rebelled, I have sinned before You, I and my family.
chunks.st: I have sinned, I have done wrong, and I have rebelled before You, I and my family.

chunks.en: Please, Hashem,
chunks.st: Please, God,

chunks.en: please forgive the sins, the rebellions and the wrongs
chunks.st: grant atonement, please, for the sins, and for the wrongs, and for the rebellions

chunks.he: שֶׁעָוִיתִי וְשֶׁפָּשַׁעְתִּי וְשֶׁחָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי,
chunks.en: that I did wrong, rebelled and sinned before You, I and my family,
chunks.st: that I have sinned, and done wrong, and rebelled before You, I and my family,

chunks.en: as it is written in the Torah of Moshe Your servant (Vayikra 16):
chunks.st: as it is written in the Torah of Moses your servant:

chunks.en: 'For on this day He will forgive you,
chunks.st: “For on this day atonement shall be made for you

chunks.he: לְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם לִפְנֵי יְיָ תִּטְהָרוּ.
chunks.en: to make you clean from all your sins; before Hashem you will be clean.'"
chunks.st: to cleanse you of all your sins; you shall be clean before the Lord” (Leviticus 16:30).

chunks.en: And they answer after him,
chunks.explain: They answer each time they hear the Kohen Gadol say Hashem's real Name.
chunks.st: And the priests and the people who were in the courtyard respond after he recites the name of God:

chunks.he: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
chunks.en: "Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
chunks.st: Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and all time.

summary: The Kohen Gadol goes to the two goats for the goral, the lottery that picks which goat is for Hashem. The lots were made of gold by Ben Gamla, and people praised him.

chunks.en: He comes to the east side of the azarah,
chunks.st: The priest then came to the eastern side of the Temple courtyard, farthest from the Holy of Holies,

chunks.en: to the north of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: to the north of the altar.

chunks.he: הַסְּגָן מִימִינוֹ וְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ.
chunks.en: the Segan on his right and the head of the family on his left.
chunks.st: The deputy was to his right, and the head of the patrilineal family belonging to the priestly watch that was assigned to serve in the Temple that week was to his left.

words.note: The Kohen who is second to the Kohen Gadol.
The head of the family of Kohanim who served that day.

chunks.en: And there are two goats there,
chunks.st: And they arranged two goats there,

chunks.he: וְקַלְפִּי הָיְתָה שָׁם וּבָהּ שְׁנֵי גוֹרָלוֹת.
chunks.en: and a box was there with two lots in it.
chunks.st: and there was a lottery receptacle there, and in it were two lots.

words.note: Two tags, one saying "for Hashem" and one saying "for Azazel."

chunks.en: They were made of boxwood,
chunks.st: These were originally made of boxwood,

words.note: A kind of wood.

chunks.en: and Ben Gamla made them of gold,
chunks.st: and the High Priest Yehoshua ben Gamla fashioned them of gold,

words.note: Yehoshua ben Gamla, a Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: and they would mention him for praise.
chunks.st: and the people would mention him favorably for what he did.
chunks.stMore: Since the mishna mentions an item designed to enhance the Temple service, it also lists other such items:

summary: This mishnah lists people who gave beautiful gifts to the Beis HaMikdash and are remembered for good: Ben Katin, King Munbaz, Queen Helene, and Nikanor.

chunks.he: בֶּן קָטִין עָשָׂה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר דַּד לַכִּיּוֹר,
chunks.en: Ben Katin made twelve spouts for the kiyor,
chunks.st: The High Priest ben Katin made twelve spigots for the basin
chunks.stMore: so that several priests could sanctify their hands and feet at once,

words.note: A Kohen Gadol.
The big copper basin the Kohanim washed their hands and feet from.

chunks.en: because it had only two.
chunks.st: as previously the basin had only two.

chunks.en: He also made a machine for the kiyor,
chunks.st: He also made a machine [mukheni] for sinking the basin into flowing water during the night

chunks.en: so that its water would not become unfit by staying overnight.
chunks.explain: The machine lowered the kiyor into the water below every night.
chunks.st: so that its water would not be disqualified by remaining overnight.
chunks.stMore: Had the water remained in the basin overnight, it would have been necessary to pour it out the following morning. By immersing the basin in flowing water, the water inside remained fit for use the next morning.

chunks.he: מֻנְבַּז הַמֶּלֶךְ הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה כָל יְדוֹת
chunks.en: King Munbaz made all the handles
chunks.st: King Munbaz would contribute the funds required to

chunks.he: הַכֵּלִים שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁל זָהָב.
chunks.en: of the Yom Kippur vessels out of gold.
chunks.st: make the handles of all the Yom Kippur vessels of gold.

chunks.en: Helene his mother made a lamp
chunks.st: Queen Helene, his mother, fashioned a

chunks.he: שֶׁל זָהָב עַל פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל.
chunks.en: of gold over the doorway of the Heichal.
chunks.st: decorative gold chandelier above the entrance of the Sanctuary.

words.note: The holy building inside the azarah, where the Menorah stood.

chunks.he: וְאַף הִיא עָשְׂתָה טַבְלָא שֶׁל זָהָב
chunks.en: She also made a tablet of gold
chunks.st: She also fashioned a golden tablet [tavla]

chunks.en: with the Torah section of Sotah written on it.
chunks.st: on which the Torah portion relating to sota was written.
chunks.stMore: The tablet could be utilized to copy this Torah portion, so that a Torah scroll need not be taken out for that purpose.

words.note: A part of the Torah in Bamidbar 5.

chunks.en: For Nikanor, miracles happened to his doors,
chunks.explain: The doors of the Nikanor Gate were saved by miracles.
chunks.st: With regard to Nicanor, miracles were performed to his doors, the doors in the gate of the Temple named for him, the Gate of Nicanor.

chunks.en: and they would mention them for praise.
chunks.st: And the people would mention all of those whose contributions were listed favorably.

summary: These people are remembered badly, because they did not want to teach their special skills to others. Good people are remembered for a bracha, and the names of the wicked rot away.
stIntro: Apropos the mention in the mishna of people who took action in the Temple and were mentioned favorably,

chunks.en: And these are remembered for shame:
chunks.st: the mishna lists those who took action in the Temple and were mentioned unfavorably.

chunks.en: The family of Garmu did not want
chunks.st: The craftsmen of the House of Garmu did not want to teach

chunks.en: to teach how to make the lechem hapanim.
chunks.st: the secret of the preparation of the shewbread and sought to keep the secret within their family.

chunks.en: The family of Avtinas did not want
chunks.st: The craftsmen of the House of Avtinas did not want to teach

chunks.en: to teach how to make the ketores.
chunks.st: the secret of the preparation of the incense.

chunks.en: Hugras ben Levi knew
chunks.st: Also, Hugras ben Levi knew

chunks.en: a special way of singing, and did not want to teach it.
chunks.st: a chapter in the art of music, as will be explained, and he did not want to teach it to others.

chunks.en: Ben Kamtzar did not want
chunks.st: And the scribe ben Kamtzar did not want to teach

chunks.en: to teach his special way of writing.
chunks.explain: He could write a four-letter word all at once.
chunks.st: a special act of writing.
chunks.stMore: He was expert at writing all four letters of a four-letter name simultaneously.

chunks.en: About the first ones it says (Mishlei 10),
chunks.st: About the first ones, who were mentioned favorably, it is stated:

chunks.en: "The memory of a tzaddik is for a bracha."
chunks.st: “The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing” (Proverbs 10:7);

chunks.en: And about these it says (there),
chunks.st: and about these who were concerned only for themselves it is stated:

chunks.en: "And the name of the wicked will rot."
chunks.st: “But the name of the wicked shall rot” (Proverbs 10:7).
